title: Bramble's Big Cool-Down
markdown:
The sun blasted. Elin practically sweated through her science shirt. The day felt like an oven with a grudge. Then a weak bark. Bramble. Her heart leaped the wrong way. The little seal pup lay like a sun-baked rug. Fur stuck. Breathing in tiny puffs. He looked cooked. Seals could overheat. This was bad. Eyes glassy. Panic prickled, then she put it in a box labelled later.

She grabbed a towel, dashed to the water, soaked it, draped it over him. Flippers like hot stones. Not enough. The towel warmed as if it had taken his side.

Dr. Ada Brook’s jeep crunched to a stop. Sharp eyes locked on the pup. “Elin. Serious trouble.” She knelt. “Gums pale. Flippers like hot stones. He’s trying to pump blood to the surface to lose heat, but the engine is overheating. Circulation is key. If it can’t dump the heat, it’s a losing battle.”

Brook watched the laboured breathing. “Kidneys struggle, flushing what they can. Lungs gasp, but breathing hot air won’t cool him. We don’t sweat like humans. Cooling comes from evaporation and breath — vapour pulling heat away. He needs rapid cooling. Now.”

Elin’s mind sparked. Evaporation. Water turning to vapour pulls heat. “The station’s misting system. Super-fine spray. Tons of droplets.”

“Yes. And keep him hydrated. Fresh water for those kidneys.”

They dashed. Elin adjusted nozzles to a whisper-fine mist that beaded on her own arms and immediately made her believe in physics again. Brook guided Bramble onto a cool tarp. The fog settled on him like a blessing with a maintenance contract. Slowly the panting lessened. His body shuddered, a tremor of relief, not panic.

“He’s responding.”

Brook watched the breathing deepen. “The mist evaporates, pulling heat away. Like sweating, faster, without the glands.” She stroked his head. “Evaporative cooling. Water to vapour takes energy — heat — from him.”

Bramble blinked, obsidian eyes focusing. A weak tail flick that Elin decided to call applause.

Brook smiled, a brilliant beam that did not need a slogan. “Circulation, breathing, kidneys — they could work once we boosted the cooler. A tuned machine, not a miracle.” She looked at Elin. “You applied what you learned. That is the useful part.”

Elin’s chest buzzed. Bramble was going to be okay. The heat felt less like a threat and more like a variable with a mist setting. She did not declare a spectacular success or the start of ocean adventures. She logged gums / flippers / mist minutes, refilled the water dish, and sat in the evaporative fog until Bramble’s bark had a joke in it again. Brook turned the jeep’s AC toward the tarp, which was cheating, and also science.
characters: Bramble (overheated seal pup), Elin (marine science student)
author: StoryGen Community
